items.title: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang as CEO two weeks after he quit
items.what_happened: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on 23 November. He had resigned on 12 November after reports of an affair with a woman US intelligence suspects of spying for China.
confirmed_facts: The board voted unanimously and the return took effect immediately, Nvidia's filing with the SEC says.
The board said senior US officials told it the return poses no national security risk.
Nvidia set up a board committee on national security and export controls and is hiring a new compliance chief.
Colette Kress served as interim CEO and stays on as finance chief.
items.why_it_matters: Nvidia makes most of the chips used to train AI, so who leads it matters for the whole AI industry. The U-turn also raises questions about board independence and political pressure.
items.context: Huang co-founded Nvidia and led it for 33 years. President Trump publicly backed his return. US lawmakers plan to question him in early December about whether advanced chips reached China.
items.analysis: Interpretation: critics quoted by Reuters say the reversal casts doubt on the board's independence. Investors first cheered, then sold, which suggests the governance worries have not gone away.
items.uncertainty: The board's own investigation is still running. What US officials told the board has not been made public.
items.what_to_watch: Huang's hearings in Congress, set for 1 and 3 December, and the findings of the board's investigation.

items.title: AI stocks slide again and Anthropic falls below its IPO price
items.what_happened: Tech shares fell on 24 November after Monday's rally on Huang's return. Nvidia dropped about 9% and Anthropic slipped below its $83 IPO price in its fourth day of trading.
confirmed_facts: Nvidia shares fell 9% on Tuesday after their biggest rally in over two decades, Mint reported.
Anthropic fell about 8%, to below its $83 IPO price, CNBC reported.
Reuters said Anthropic was on track to lose nearly $200 billion in value.
The Nasdaq rose about 6% on 23 November, then fell on 24 November, Economic Times reported.
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic's listing was the biggest IPO on record. How its shares trade is a live test of whether investors believe AI firms can earn back their huge costs.
items.context: Anthropic listed on 19 November at $83 a share. It rose above $111 on day one before settling near $97, Futurism reported. AI stocks have swung hard all month.
items.analysis: Interpretation: moves this large in a few days suggest investors are unsure how to value AI companies that grow fast but still lose money.
items.uncertainty: Daily price moves are noisy. A week of trading says little about long-term value.
items.what_to_watch: Whether Anthropic regains its IPO price, and US inflation data due this week.

items.title: US blacklists Megaspeed, the chip firm at the centre of the Nvidia scandal
items.what_happened: The US added Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company, to its export control list. The firm is accused of funnelling AI chips to China.
confirmed_facts: Megaspeed was added to a US export control list, The Hindu reported on 24 November.
Megaspeed has been accused of funnelling AI chips to China, the BBC reported.
Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, had a relationship with Jensen Huang. They are not related.
US authorities are investigating Megaspeed and Alice Huang, CNBC reported.
items.why_it_matters: Export controls are the main US tool to limit China's access to advanced AI chips. The case shows how chips can leak through companies in third countries.
items.context: Earlier reports said the Commerce Department had held off listing Megaspeed. The listing came the same day Nvidia brought Huang back.
items.uncertainty: Megaspeed's response and the number of chips involved were not clear in the reports we saw.
items.what_to_watch: Whether more firms are listed and whether Nvidia faces any penalty over chips that reached China.

items.title: US jury finds Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets
items.what_happened: A US jury in New York found Huawei guilty of conspiring to steal trade secrets on 24 November. It acquitted the Chinese company of racketeering.
confirmed_facts: The verdict followed a months-long trial in New York, the BBC reported.
The jury acquitted Huawei of the racketeering charge, the BBC reported.
Prosecutors also accused Huawei of business in sanctioned countries such as Iran and North Korea, The Hindu reported.
items.why_it_matters: It is a landmark case in the US-China tech rivalry. The verdict may shape how other countries judge Huawei's telecom equipment.
items.context: The trial came after nearly a decade of legal fights between Huawei and US prosecutors, the South China Morning Post reported.
items.uncertainty: Penalties and whether Huawei will appeal were not in the reports we saw.
items.what_to_watch: Sentencing or fines, any appeal, and China's official response.

items.title: Indian markets shut for Guru Nanak Jayanti after Monday's sharp fall
items.what_happened: NSE and BSE were closed on 24 November for Guru Nanak Jayanti. On 23 November the Sensex fell 1,484 points and the Nifty closed at 25,349.65, dragged by banks.
confirmed_facts: The 1,484-point fall on 23 November was the Sensex's worst day in over four months, The Shillong Times reported.
The rupee fell 30 paise to 92.92 per dollar on 23 November, ending a five-day rally, The Hindu reported.
Brent crude settled at $91.40 on 24 November, up over 2%, Forbes Middle East reported.
The Nasdaq and S&P 500 ended lower on 24 November as Nvidia fell, Economic Times reported.
items.why_it_matters: A weak rupee and oil near $90 raise India's import bill and inflation risk. Big daily swings show how closely Indian stocks now track global AI moves.
items.context: Even after Monday's fall, the Sensex is up about 11% in November, BusinessLine reported. Foreign investors bought for a 16th straight session, Kotak Neo reported.
items.uncertainty: Reports cite bank selling and global swings in AI stocks for Monday's fall. Their relative weight is unclear.
items.what_to_watch: How Indian markets reopen on 25 November after Wall Street's moves, and whether the rupee holds near 93.

items.title: US prepares new tariffs on India, China and others over subsidies
items.what_happened: The Trump administration is preparing new tariffs on India, China and other economies over industrial subsidies and excess factory capacity. An announcement is expected this week, Mint and Reuters reported.
confirmed_facts: Reuters, citing sources, said the tariffs would follow a probe into excess factory capacity.
Mint said China, India and 15 other economies could be hit. India Today put the number at 16 nations.
The US opened Section 301 trade probes into 16 economies, including India and China, in March 2026.
items.why_it_matters: New US duties would hit Indian exporters while the rupee is weak and India is racing to close trade deals elsewhere.
items.context: Section 301 lets the US act against trade practices it sees as unfair. The probes began after a court setback for Trump's earlier tariffs, Business Today reported.
items.uncertainty: Rates, products and the final list of countries have not been announced. Reports differ on how many economies are covered.
items.what_to_watch: The formal announcement, the rate set for India, and New Delhi's response.

items.title: India and Canada near a trade pact ahead of a Modi visit
items.what_happened: India and Canada are 'very close' to concluding trade talks, an Indian official said. The Globe and Mail reported the two are also negotiating defence and information security pacts before a Modi visit.
confirmed_facts: Both sides aim to conclude the talks by the end of this year, The Hindu reported on 24 November.
Canada's High Commissioner said the text was close to final and expected Modi to visit in December, Business Today reported.
The two countries agreed a uranium supply deal in March 2026, Al Jazeera reported.
items.why_it_matters: A deal would cap a turnaround after the 2023 diplomatic row. It would also give India another trade partner as US tariffs loom.
items.context: Ties collapsed in 2023 and have recovered since Mark Carney became Canada's prime minister, Canada's envoy said.
items.uncertainty: Ratification will take longer because Canadian provinces are involved. Visit dates are not public.
items.what_to_watch: Modi's visit to Canada and whether a trade text or defence pact is signed there.

items.title: India's aid to Nepal put at $1.6 billion after Shah's visit
items.what_happened: India pledged $1.6 billion to Nepal during Prime Minister Balendra Shah's visit, the BBC and Al Jazeera reported. Nepal also secured port access and a new train service.
confirmed_facts: Al Jazeera described the $1.6 billion as flood relief for Nepal.
The BBC said Shah set contentious issues aside to secure funding, port access and a new train.
India's foreign secretary called the Eminent Persons Group report on boundary issues 'not relevant', ThePrint reported.
India plans an offshore IIT campus in Nepal, ET Education reported.
items.why_it_matters: Yesterday's reports differed on the package size. The $1.6 billion figure now has two outlets behind it, while the border question stays open.
items.context: Nepal is rebuilding after deadly floods in August 2026. The new Ayodhya to Janakpur train was flagged off during the visit.
items.uncertainty: How the $1.6 billion splits between grants, loans and projects was not clear in the reports we saw.
items.what_to_watch: Disbursement timelines and whether Nepal presses India on the boundary report.

items.title: Government warns WhatsApp Web sessions can be hijacked
items.what_happened: India's cybercrime agency warned that WhatsApp Web accounts left logged in on public computers can be hijacked. The Centre also told staff to avoid WhatsApp Web for government and sensitive work, the Indian Express reported.
confirmed_facts: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit issued the advisory, The Hindu reported.
It asks users to log out manually after every session.
The unit is part of the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C).
items.why_it_matters: WhatsApp is how most Indians and many offices communicate. A hijacked account can be used to defraud a person's contacts.
items.context: WhatsApp Web mirrors a phone's chats in a browser. Anyone who later uses a shared computer with a live session can read and send messages.
items.uncertainty: The advisory did not say how many accounts have been hijacked this way.
items.what_to_watch: Whether ministries issue formal rules on messaging apps for official work.

items.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre's reply on the 11-year delay in judges' appointment rules
items.what_happened: The Supreme Court sought replies from the Centre and its own Secretary General on a plea to finalise the Memorandum of Procedure for appointing judges. The plea also wants collegium minutes under RTI.
confirmed_facts: Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale issued notice on 18 November, LiveLaw reported.
The plea was filed by the NGO Lok Prahari.
A revised memorandum has been pending for nearly 11 years, since the 2015 NJAC judgment.
Justice PS Narasimha had earlier recused from hearing the case.
items.why_it_matters: The memorandum sets how judges are chosen and how fast. Delays and secrecy in appointments affect court backlogs and public trust.
items.context: In 2015 the Supreme Court struck down the NJAC law and kept the collegium system. It asked for a revised memorandum, which is still not final. The original dates from 1999.
items.uncertainty: It is unclear when the Centre will reply or whether the court will set a deadline.
items.what_to_watch: The Centre's reply and the next hearing date.

items.title: Tata Sons board meeting on RBI listing pushed to 30 November
items.what_happened: A key Tata Sons board meeting was postponed to 30 November after Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata raised concerns, The Hindu reported. It will discuss the RBI-mandated listing of Tata Sons.
confirmed_facts: The meeting was earlier set for 26 November, Business Today reported.
A 16 November RBI letter told Tata Sons to follow rules for upper-layer NBFCs, including listing.
Tata Trusts owns 66% of Tata Sons and is divided over a listing.
The Shapoorji Pallonji group, which owns 18.4%, wants Tata Sons to buy back shares.
items.why_it_matters: Tata Sons controls India's largest business group. A listing would be one of India's biggest and would change how the group is run.
items.context: The RBI classes Tata Sons as an upper-layer NBFC, which has a three-year window to list. Noel Tata has pushed to challenge the RBI order or restructure to avoid it.
items.analysis: Interpretation: the delay suggests the boardroom split over listing is not yet resolved.
items.uncertainty: The exact concerns Noel Tata raised were not fully reported.
items.what_to_watch: The 30 November board meeting and any legal challenge to the RBI order.

items.title: China opens corruption probe into Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
items.what_happened: China announced a corruption investigation into Chen Jining, the Communist Party secretary of Shanghai and a member of the Politburo, The Hindu reported on 24 November.
confirmed_facts: Chen had been expected to take a top leadership role in 2027, The Hindu reported.
He became Shanghai party chief in 2022 after serving as Beijing mayor, Bloomberg reported at the time.
items.why_it_matters: Shanghai's party chief is one of China's most senior posts. A probe at this level could reshape who rises at the 2027 party congress.
items.context: Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign has removed many senior officials. Few sitting Politburo members have been placed under investigation.
items.uncertainty: The specific allegations against Chen have not been made public.
items.what_to_watch: Whether Chen is formally removed from his posts, and who is named to run Shanghai.

items.title: Three tankers hit mines in Hormuz as US widens Iran sanctions
items.what_happened: Iran said three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, despite US escorts. The US Treasury widened sanctions on Iran's financial networks, CNBC reported.
confirmed_facts: Iran said three tankers hit mines in Hormuz, CNBC reported on 24 November.
The US sanctioned dozens of people and firms linked to Iran's shadow banking networks, Reuters reported.
Iran's rial hit a record low after the new sanctions, Anadolu reported.
Oil traffic through Hormuz is down 40%, Al Jazeera reported.
items.why_it_matters: Hormuz is a key route for the Gulf oil India relies on. Attacks there raise shipping and insurance costs and keep oil prices jumpy.
items.context: The US and Iran are at war in 2026. Iran says it will use 'all available means' to counter a US blockade, Al Arabiya reported.
items.uncertainty: Iran's account of the mine strikes had not been independently confirmed in the reports we saw.
items.what_to_watch: Oil prices, shipping insurance rates and any move toward US-Iran talks.

items.title: First industry-built PSLV slips to early 2027, ISRO says Gaganyaan on track
items.what_happened: The maiden flight of PSLV-N1, the first PSLV built fully by industry, is delayed again to early next year. ISRO's chief said the Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme is not delayed and is in its final phase.
confirmed_facts: The PSLV-N1 maiden flight is now likely early next year, the Indian Express reported.
A consortium of HAL and L&T has been given five PSLV missions, India Today reported.
ISRO's chief said Gaganyaan preparations are in the final phase, News18 reported.
items.why_it_matters: Handing rocket building to industry frees ISRO for harder work like human spaceflight. Gaganyaan would be India's first crewed mission.
items.context: ISRO has said the first crewed Gaganyaan flight is targeted for 2027, after uncrewed test flights.
items.uncertainty: No firm dates were given for PSLV-N1 or for the first crewed flight.
items.what_to_watch: A launch date for PSLV-N1 and the next uncrewed Gaganyaan test.

items.title: BepiColombo enters orbit around Mercury despite a glitch
items.what_happened: The European and Japanese spacecraft BepiColombo has begun orbiting Mercury, The Hindu reported. European Spaceflight said a software glitch was reported during arrival.
confirmed_facts: BepiColombo began its orbit of Mercury, The Hindu reported.
A 'software glitch' was reported, European Spaceflight said.
The mission will study why Mercury has a magnetic field and why ice exists in its sun-scorched polar craters.
items.why_it_matters: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun. Studying it helps explain how rocky planets form near their star and keep magnetic fields.
items.context: The mission will also look at strange surface depressions on Mercury called hollows.
items.uncertainty: How serious the glitch is was not clear in the reports we saw.
items.what_to_watch: Whether the glitch delays the start of science observations.

items.title: Gaza declares a meningitis epidemic alert
items.what_happened: Gaza's health ministry issued an epidemic alert after a sharp rise in meningitis, with 272 new infections in October, the Guardian reported.
confirmed_facts: October's 272 cases are more than eight times the normal monthly rate, the ministry said.
Oxfam says Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into a 'toxic wasteland', the BBC reported.
An Israeli strike on 24 November killed Hamas's internal security chief, the BBC reported.
items.why_it_matters: Meningitis spreads fast in crowded shelters and can kill quickly without treatment. The rise points to how damaged Gaza's water, sanitation and health care are.
items.context: A ceasefire has been in place for over a year, but strikes continue. Gaza authorities say they recorded 6,405 Israeli violations in 410 days, Anadolu reported.
items.uncertainty: Case counts come from Gaza's health ministry and are hard to verify independently.
items.what_to_watch: Whether vaccines and treatment reach Gaza, and November's case numbers.

items.title: Explainer: what AI chips are and why Nvidia's lead
items.what_happened: The Conversation published an explainer on what AI chips are and why Nvidia's dominate, as Huang's return shook markets.
confirmed_facts: Nvidia was the dominant seller of graphics chips by the early 2000s, the article says.
Those graphics chips later turned out to be well suited for running AI.
items.why_it_matters: Nvidia's leadership drama moved stock markets worldwide this week. Knowing what its chips do explains why.
items.context: Graphics chips do many simple sums at the same time. Training AI models needs huge amounts of exactly that kind of maths.
items.analysis: The author's main point: Nvidia was in the right place at the right time, and its graphics chips became the engine of modern AI.
items.what_to_watch: Rivals building their own chips, such as Amazon with its reported $7.5 billion Decart deal.

items.title: Explainer: a claimed AI proof of the Riemann hypothesis that no human can read
items.what_happened: The Conversation examines a claimed AI-assisted solution to the Riemann hypothesis that runs to 17 million lines of code, and asks whether it is right.
confirmed_facts: The claimed solution runs to 17 million lines of code, the article says.
In October, OpenAI announced an AI proof of a weaker 'quasi' version of the hypothesis, Quanta Magazine reported.
Mathematician Peter Sarnak told Quanta he will not treat that result as a theorem until humans check every detail.
items.why_it_matters: The Riemann hypothesis is one of maths' most famous open problems. A proof no person can follow would change what it means to know a result is true.
items.context: The hypothesis is about where the zeros of the zeta function lie. Those zeros are tied to how prime numbers are spread out.
items.analysis: The article's question: can a proof checked only by machines be trusted, and what do mathematicians lose if they cannot read it?
items.uncertainty: The claim has not been accepted by mathematicians. We could not open the article itself, only its summary.
items.what_to_watch: Whether independent mathematicians or formal proof checkers confirm the claim.

items.title: Explainer: why the Trump, Xi and Putin Shenzhen declaration matters
items.what_happened: Indian Express Explained looks at the peace declaration Trump, Xi and Putin issued in Shenzhen on 19 November, and why it matters.
confirmed_facts: The three leaders reaffirmed that a nuclear war should never be fought, Reuters reported.
They pledged to advance UN reform and raise supplies of refined fuels for all countries.
They pledged to uphold the immunity of state officials in international courts.
items.why_it_matters: It came from an unprecedented three-way summit of nuclear powers. It could shape arms control and UN reform debates that matter to India.
items.context: The summit was held alongside APEC in Shenzhen. The three countries remain deeply divided over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade, Reuters said.
items.analysis: An SCMP analysis said the declaration made the summit look more like a photo op than a breakthrough. Smaller countries fear being sidelined, Reuters reported.
items.uncertainty: The declaration has no detailed commitments or timelines in the reports we saw.
items.what_to_watch: Whether US, Russian and Chinese officials start formal talks on nuclear risks.

notes: Explained items: 19 across 10 sections. Briefs: 30. Web search returned few same-day pages, so several items cite candidate article URLs from the fetched feeds (not fetched by us) and cross-check across outlets in the candidates. Fetched and read: Nvidia SEC filing, LiveLaw, Business Today (Tata, Canada), Quanta, Scientific American, BusinessDay (Reuters on Shenzhen), Futurism, Longbridge. The Conversation Riemann article was not opened. Its facts come from the feed summary. Indian markets were shut on 24 November, so the markets item uses 23 November closes. Climate and society had real news but nothing new enough for a full item, so they have briefs only. Air India's CEO change and Lula's re-election were skipped as not new. The Anthropic item is written only from third-party reports.
